says: When the filter dialog is confirmed with 'Supported on' ticked, a product filter is created even if no product is ticked; an empty product list is a filter, not 'no restriction'. When it is unticked, no product filter is created and both matching options are dropped.

A product filter keeps a policy only when the ticked products meet its support definition: an entry naming a ticked product is met, and an entry naming a version range of a parent product is met when a ticked product lies in that range. With no product ticked, no entry is met, so only policies the blank-support option admits can pass.

The option 'Match a policy if at least one selected product is supported' decides how a support definition with several entries is met. Ticked, a definition marked 'all of' needs every entry met. Unticked, one met entry is enough for any definition. The label reads as the unticked case, so the labelled wording and the behaviour differ.

The option 'Match policies with missing or blank support definitions' decides policies with no support information. Ticked, policies with no support definition, a blank one, or an entry naming no product pass the product filter. Unticked, they are refused.
When the filter dialog opens with a filter that has no product restriction, 'Supported on' is unticked, no product is ticked, and both matching options are ticked.

Reset returns every choice in the filter dialog to its starting value: policy type, current state and commented go back to Any, 'Supported on' is unticked, no product is ticked and both matching options are ticked. Nothing is applied until OK.

Find by Registry does not check its patterns when Search is pressed. Value names and keys are matched with the Visual Basic Like operator, which rejects a malformed pattern such as a value name with an unclosed '[' by raising an error when a policy's values are tested.

The search task in the results dialog has no handling for an error raised by the search function, so an invalid pattern in Find by Registry ends the task without a finishing message or any change to the dialog.

When a value name is entered in Find by Registry, a value counts only when its whole name matches, ignoring letter case. The match uses the Like operator: '*' is any text, '?' one character, '#' one digit, '[abc]' one listed character and '[!abc]' one not listed. A '#' or '[' is not literal.

When the key text holds '*' or '?', the whole key path must match it as a Like pattern, ignoring letter case; '#' and '[...]' keep their Like meanings there. A key with only '#' or '[' and no '*' or '?' is not a pattern: it is treated as a literal path or folder name.
When Search succeeds in Find by Registry, after the two refusals pass, the search function is kept for the results dialog and the dialog closes as accepted, which starts the search.

When Search is pressed in Find by Text with empty text, nothing is searched and the person is told "Please enter search terms." The check is for empty text, not blank text: text of only spaces is accepted and matches only texts that are empty or hold two separators in a row, such as a double space or a line break.

The search text is split on spaces only into plain words, wildcard words (containing '*' or '?') and quoted phrases. A word starting with a double quote opens a phrase and is not checked for a closing quote, so "foo" alone stays open. The phrase ends at a later word ending with a double quote. '*' and '?' inside a phrase are plain characters.

A quoted phrase that is never closed is dropped with every word after its opening quote. This includes one quoted word such as "foo" with no later word ending in a quote, so searching for it alone leaves no terms. With no terms, every title and every comment text counts as a hit, and so does a description (an absent description reads as empty text).

A piece of text is a hit only when every plain word is a whole word in it, every wildcard word matches some whole word, and every quoted phrase appears as consecutive whole words. Words are split on spaces, carriage returns and line feeds, not tabs. Wildcards use the Like operator after cleanup, so '#' means one digit but '[' and ']' are stripped and lists cannot be used.
When Search succeeds in Find by Text, after the two refusals pass, the search function is kept for the results dialog and the dialog closes as accepted, which starts the search.

Find Next returns the result after the one last chosen and starts from the first if none was chosen. The chosen position is set by Go or double-click on a row, and by each Find Next. At the end of the list, with no search, or past the results listed so far while a search runs, it returns nothing.
Re-opening Search Results without a new search never reruns or resumes a search; a search stopped by Stop or by closing stays stopped with the partial results it had.
Pressing Escape in Import REG closes it as cancelled.
When Import REG is opened, the REG file and prefix boxes are emptied, so no earlier entry carries over.
Pressing Escape in Import SPOL closes it as cancelled, unless text in the focused text box is selected, in which case Escape does nothing.
When Import SPOL is shown, any SPOL result kept from an earlier use is cleared, so only a new Apply can hand one back.
Open File in Import SPOL offers .spol files first, then all files. Picking a file replaces the whole text box with its contents with no confirmation. Cancelling the picker changes nothing.

When an ID is typed in Find by ID, only surrounding spaces are ignored and the ID must match letter case exactly. It is looked up as category, then product, then support definition, then policy; the first kind found is selected.

When an ID is typed in Find by ID, the selected policy, category, product and support are cleared before the lookup, but the user or computer section choice is not, so an earlier section stays held after a different or no match. It matters only for a selected policy.
